title: fix(i18n): deep-merge createI18n resources so a partial group override keeps the group
body:
Fixes #7572

`createI18n` merged `resources` over the built-in packs **one level deep**, but a
language pack's top-level keys ARE the namespace groups (`common`, `calendar`,
`list`, ...), each a nested object. Supplying a partial group therefore
**replaced** it:

```ts
createI18n({ defaultLanguage: 'en', resources: { en: { calendar: { today: 'Heute' } } } });
```

left `calendar.today` set and dropped `month` / `week` / `day` / `allDay` /
`newEvent` / `moreEvents` / `unscheduled` from the instance. `t('calendar.allDay')`
then returned the bare key, and `calendar.allDay` reached the DOM as literal
text — silently, with no error and no warning.

Route **A** per the dispatch: the merge now recurses. Route B (refusing a partial
group override) is breaking on a published API and is not attempted here.

## 1. Census first — who passes a partial group?

Measured before the fix, not after. A probe parsed every `resources` object
literal in the repo (6267 tracked files, 47 literals, aliases and shorthand
resolved), classified each `(language, top-level key)` against the built-in pack
for that language, and reported anything it could not resolve rather than
dropping it.

**A zero would have been meaningless without a control, so the probe was first
run against a fixture of planted positives** — the card's exact shape, an
alias-indirected variant, a deeper partial, a scalar-for-object clash and a
dynamic value. All five were classified as expected, including one the fixture
itself had mislabelled as a full override (supplying `capability.group` does drop
`capability.label.*`). The instrument demonstrably fires.

| Verdict | Sites | Affected by this change? |
|---|---|---|
| `PARTIAL_OVERRIDE` | **2** | yes — both repaired, see below |
| `ADD_GROUP` | 20 | no — key absent from the pack |
| `NEW_LANGUAGE` | 3 | no — `th`, `pt-BR`; no built-in pack |
| `TYPE_CLASH` | 0 | — |
| `UNRESOLVED` (dynamic) | 21 | all resolved by hand, none a partial override |

**No caller depends on replacement semantics.** Both partial-override sites are
victims of the defect, and the fix repairs them without touching either file:

- `packages/plugin-gantt/demo/main.tsx:645` supplies 53 of the 80 `zh.gantt.*`
  keys and silently loses the other 27 (`toolbar.refresh`, `row.open`,
  `menu.searchTasks`, `delete.*`, ...). Its own comment says the demo "is never
  half-translated" — today it is exactly that.
- `skills/objectui/guides/i18n.md:14`, the documented way to use this API, drops
  46 of the 48 `common.*` keys in **both** `en` and `zh`.

The 21 unresolved sites were read individually: 10 are `packages/plugin-grid/demo`
handing back the built-in packs themselves (identity-checked: `resources.en ===
builtInLocales.en`, so a no-op either way), 2 are the provider's async
`addResourceBundle` path, 1 is `UserFilters`' `crm` bundle (an added group), and
the rest are prose, comments or an unrelated `resources` (YAML frontmatter,
`performance.getEntriesByType`, gantt's assignable resources). The sibling
`objectstack` repo has no `createI18n` call sites at all.

## 2. The array question, answered explicitly

**Arrays are replaced, not concatenated.**

This is stated because it is a decision, not a library default — an unstated
choice here is the very shape this card is about. Measured: **no built-in pack
carries an array value today** (every leaf in all ten packs is a string, checked
by walking the loaded packs, not by grep), so nothing observable rides on it. The
rule decides what a *future* array means.

Replacement is the only rule that lets an author shorten or reorder a list they
are overriding, and the only one that stays idempotent when the merge runs again.
Concatenation makes a list impossible to shrink and grows it on every merge.

This is deliberately **narrower than i18next's own `deepExtend`** (i18next
26.4.0, `dist/cjs/i18next.js:93`), which the provider's async
`addResourceBundle(lang, 'translation', resources, true, true)` path uses: that
recurses into arrays index-wise, so a 2-element override onto a 5-element base
leaves the base's last 3 entries behind. That stale hybrid is the same
silent-surprise class this fix removes, so the sync path does not copy it. The
two paths are observably identical for every value shape that exists today
(strings all the way down); they would differ only for an array, which no pack
has. Worth knowing when one is added.

`__proto__` is skipped. The merge assigns recursively where the old code spread,
and assignment — unlike object spread — reaches the prototype setter; i18next's
`deepExtend` guards the same key. Pinned by a test.

## 3. The test split

`packages/i18n/src/__tests__/i18n.test.ts` had one test named
`merges custom resources with built-in locales` that supplied `custom` — a key no
pack has — and then asserted `common.save`, a **different** group. So it pinned
only *adding* a group; the merge never had to survive a collision. That
mis-naming is why this defect read as already-covered.

It is now two tests named for the operation each pins, plus four more:

| Test | Pins |
|---|---|
| `adds a NEW top-level group and leaves the built-in groups intact` | the old assertions, honestly named |
| `overrides ONE key of an EXISTING group and keeps that group's other keys` | **the defect** — all seven `calendar.*` siblings survive |
| `merges below the group level, not just one level deeper` | `capability.group.platform`, three deep — a fixed "one more level" would still drop siblings |
| `replaces an array value instead of concatenating it` | the array decision above |
| `re-supplying an identical built-in pack changes nothing` | the `plugin-grid/demo` shape |
| `does not let a resource key reach Object.prototype` | the `__proto__` guard |

The override test also asserts the failure mode directly
(`expect(t('calendar.allDay')).not.toBe('calendar.allDay')`), so it fails the way
the bug presented rather than only on the happy value.

## Verification

Reverse-verified by ablation, from a committed state: reverting `i18n.ts` to the
shallow merge turns the new tests red, and restoring it turns them green — with
the on-disk mutation and the byte-exact restore both proved, not assumed. Numbers
and command output are in the report comment on #7572.

Not folded in: **#7567** (the gate-blindness half of #7454) — looked at, left
alone. The `t('calendar.allDay')` ternary #7454 removed is **not** restored: it
guarded one of seven labels, so in the scenario it protected the other six
already rendered raw keys. The coherent fix is the one in this PR.
